Safety Review Committee packet: Study CP-101, Cohort 4

A worked example on synthetic data. Study CP-101 does not exist, and this is not a study document.

Prepared

25 October 2026

Synthetic data, worked example. Every number below is computed from the TRIALMON synthetic dataset by the same R functions that drive the TRIALMON console. In a real study the tables a committee relies on come from validated programs on ADaM; this packet was not produced by a validated system, and no one has signed it. The packet presents data. It makes no recommendation: the committee adjudicates and decides, and records its decision in the minutes.

Item Detail
Study CP-101 (synthetic): first-in-human, multiple ascending dose, open label for illustration
Design Once-daily oral dosing, Days 1 to 28 (the DLT window); follow-up to Day 43
Data cut After the last Cohort 4 participant completed the DLT window (Day 29)
Cohorts dosed C1 10 mg (n=3), C2 30 mg (n=3), C3 60 mg (n=6), C4 120 mg (n=6); 18 participants dosed. Cohort 5 (200 mg) is planned and not dosed.
Settings (SAP parameters) MedDRA v29.1; NCI CTCAE v6.0 for lab grades (AE grades as recorded, v6.0); potential Hy’s Law window 30 days; ALP < 2x ULN convention off
Status Draft for committee review. Rendered from synthetic data; not a validated output.

Questions for the committee

  1. Adjudicate a candidate DLT. CP101-018 (Cohort 4, 120 mg) had QTcF 503 ms on Day 22 (baseline 462 ms). Under the synthetic protocol, QTcF above 500 ms is a candidate DLT; the event has not been adjudicated (Sections 5 and 9).
  2. Review the liver findings. CP101-014 (an adjudicated DLT) meets the potential Hy’s Law screen; CP101-004 and CP101-009 had ALT or AST above 3x ULN that needed confirmation (Section 4).
  3. Decide the next step for dose escalation from the options the protocol allows (Section 9). No option is recommended here.

Liver tests

Definition used. A participant is a potential Hy’s Law case when ALT or AST is at least 3x ULN and total bilirubin (TBL) is above 2x ULN on or after the day of that aminotransferase elevation, within 30 days of it (the window is an SAP convention). Every draw with ALT or AST at least 3x ULN opens its own window, so a second elevation weeks after the first is screened as well; the tables report the first draw that qualifies. ALP is shown but not used to exclude a case; the SAP option ALP < 2x ULN is off. This follows FDA, Drug-Induced Liver Injury: Premarketing Clinical Evaluation (July 2009), which asks for TBL above 2x ULN “without initial findings of cholestasis (elevated serum ALP)” and for other causes to be ruled out. The screen cannot rule out other causes; the medical monitor does. Separately, any ALT or AST above 3x ULN calls for repeat ALT, AST, ALP and TBL within 48 to 72 hours to confirm it.

eDISH: each point is one participant’s peak post-baseline ALT or AST against peak TBL. The peaks need not come from the same draw, so the upper-right quadrant is a prompt to check timing, not a classification. Lower right: aminotransferase elevation without TBL above 2x ULN. Upper left: TBL above 2x ULN without an aminotransferase elevation (cholestasis, Gilbert syndrome or other causes).

Participants with ALT or AST above 3x ULN, or in the upper-right quadrant
Participant Cohort Peak ALT / AST (x ULN) ALT or AST >= 3x (day) ALP then (x ULN) R ratio (pattern) Peak TBL (x ULN) TBL > 2x on or after it (day) Potential Hy’s Law Quadrant
CP101-014 C4 5.6 / 4.9 15 1.1 4.0 (mixed) 3.1 22 Yes Upper right
CP101-004 C2 3.3 / 2.4 22 0.8 4.1 (mixed) 2.4 No Upper right
CP101-009 C3 4.2 / 3.6 15 1.2 3.5 (mixed) 1.6 No Lower right
Confirmation of aminotransferase elevations above 3x ULN
Participant ALT or AST > 3x ULN (day) Value (x ULN) First full repeat panel (day) Days later Within 48 to 72 h Repeat ALT or AST (x ULN) FDA (2009) discontinuation consideration
CP101-004 22 3.3 24 2 Yes 2.6
CP101-009 15 4.2 20 5 No 3.4
CP101-014 15 4.4 17 2 Yes 5.1 ALT or AST > 3x ULN with TBL > 2x ULN in the same draw

ALT or AST >= 3x (day): for a potential Hy’s Law case, the draw that opens the qualifying window; otherwise the first such draw. ALP and the R ratio are read from that draw. R ratio = (ALT/ULN)/(ALP/ULN) (at the first draw with ALT at least 3x ULN if only AST reached 3x in that draw): 5 or more hepatocellular, between 2 and 5 mixed, 2 or less cholestatic. “Within 48 to 72 h” is judged on study days (the data carry days, not clock times), as 3 days or fewer. The FDA (2009) discontinuation considerations that these data can show are ALT or AST above 8x ULN, above 5x ULN for more than 2 weeks, and above 3x ULN with TBL above 2x ULN; INR and symptoms are not in these data.

CP101-006 C2 453 486 15 33 AMBER
CP101-011 C3 448 474 22 26 watch
CP101-012 C3 446 468 15 22 watch
CP101-018 C4 462 503 22 41 RED

QTcF: Fridericia-corrected QT, triplicate mean. Categories per ICH E14 (May 2005), the E14 Q&A (R3) (December 2015) and the E14/S7B Q&As (February 2022): maximum post-baseline value above 450, 480 and 500 ms, regardless of sex, and maximum increase from baseline above 30 and 60 ms. Categories are cumulative and a value equal to a threshold is not above it. Baseline: Day 1 predose; post-baseline values start at the Day 1 4 h post-dose ECG. Participants already above 450 ms at baseline: 2 of 18. A categorical summary is a screen; concentration-QTc modeling belongs in a prespecified analysis.

Participant Test Baseline grade Worst grade
CP101-014 Alanine aminotransferase increased 0 3

CP101-008 Thrombocytopenia 0 3

Lab grades: NCI CTCAE v6.0. Grades come from multiples of the ULN or LLN, or from fold over baseline where the term says so, not from absolute values alone. Creatinine increased: under v6.0, fold over baseline applies only when the baseline is below the LLN; under v5.0 the grade is the worse of the x ULN and fold-over-baseline grades. The v6.0 cut points follow admiral 1.5.0 (atoxgr_criteria_ctcv6) and were not re-checked against the NCI v6.0 workbook here; v5.0 follows the NCI v5.0 workbook (2017-11-27). Baseline grades use reference-range criteria only. Hemoglobin grade 4 is a clinical judgment and is not derived from the value.

Pre-specified acceptable ranges, as in ICH E6(R3) section 3.10.1.3 (“quality tolerance limits at the trial level”): exceeding one triggers evaluation, not an automatic stop. The operational values are synthetic. Every level in this packet rolls up worst-of: the participant and cohort tier is RED and the study tier is AMBER, so the overall screen is RED.

Participants. Potential Hy’s Law: window 30 days, ALP option off. Grade 3 or higher TEAE counts AE grades as recorded by the investigator (NCI CTCAE v6.0).

What an illustrative 3+3 rule would say (a reference, not a recommendation)
Cohort Dose (mg) Illustrative 3+3 rule reference
C1 10 0 of 3: escalation-eligible under the rule
C2 30 0 of 3: escalation-eligible under the rule
C3 60 1 of 6: escalation-eligible under the rule
C4 120 1 of 6 confirmed, 1 pending adjudication. If not a DLT: 1 of 6, escalation-eligible under the rule. If a DLT: 2 of 6, under the rule, the dose exceeds the MTD

Reading the rule reference. Under a 3+3 rule, 0 of 3 or 1 of 6 participants with a DLT is escalation-eligible, 1 of 3 means the cohort expands to 6, and 2 or more mean the dose exceeds the maximum tolerated dose; a dose can be called the MTD only with 6 participants treated at it. For Cohort 4 the reference depends on the committee’s adjudication of CP101-018. 3+3 appears here only as an illustration: model-assisted designs such as BOIN (FDA fit-for-purpose determination, December 2021, for the local BOIN design under a non-informative prior) are the current alternative, and this example implements neither as a decision tool. A rule reference never replaces the committee’s review of the whole safety picture, including the potential Hy’s Law case at 120 mg.

Options the synthetic protocol allows the committee to consider, in protocol order: escalate to 200 mg as planned; escalate to an intermediate dose; enroll further participants at 120 mg; stop escalation and select a lower dose; pause dosing pending further evaluation. They are listed, not ranked.

Methods and conventions

  • Source. The TRIALMON synthetic dataset (adsl, adlb, adeg, adae, cohorts, study_kri), written by R/gen_data.R from one seed. Every table is computed at render time by R/logic.R, the code behind the TRIALMON console and its tests, and the findings the text cites (participants, values, days and counts) are computed from the same objects. The study design and the protocol’s options are fixed text from the synthetic protocol.
  • Populations. Safety population: all dosed participants. Baseline: the Day 1 predose value. Post-baseline: labs after Day 1; ECGs from the Day 1 4 h post-dose time point on; both include unscheduled draws.
  • Counting. Participants are counted once per row of a table. Percentages use the dosed participants in the column.
  • Dictionaries and grading. MedDRA v29.1; NCI CTCAE v6.0 for laboratory grades, derived from the values; AE grades as recorded by the investigator under NCI CTCAE v6.0 (a property of the data: changing the lab-grading version does not re-grade an AE). All three are parameters of this document (meddra_version, ctcae_version, ae_ctcae_version), as are the Hy’s Law window (hys_window_days) and the ALP convention (alp_convention).
  • Guidance cited. FDA, Drug-Induced Liver Injury: Premarketing Clinical Evaluation (July 2009); ICH E14 (May 2005), E14 Q&A (R3) (10 Dec 2015) and E14/S7B Q&As (Step 4 21 Feb 2022); NCI CTCAE v6.0; ICH E6(R3) (Step 4 6 Jan 2025; EU effective 23 Jul 2025; FDA final guidance Sep 2025); Annex 2 Step 4 3 Jun 2026 (CHMP 25 Jun 2026, EU effective 15 Jan 2027; FDA: draft guidance Dec 2024, not final).
  • What was executed. Rendered with Quarto and R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24) on synthetic data; the rules are covered by testthat tests (rule boundaries, the shipped study and the Shiny server). No validated system or independent programmer produced or checked these numbers.
  • What a real packet adds. Tables from validated programs on ADaM, a named statistician’s sign-off, and, for a DSMB with access to unblinded comparisons, open and closed sections with an independent reporting statistician. This open-label example has no closed section.

```{r setup}
library(ggplot2)
source("../trialmon_shiny/R/logic.R")
source("_report-helpers.R")
tm <- trialmon_load("../trialmon_shiny/data")
S <- trialmon_settings(params$ctcae_version, params$hys_window_days, params$alp_convention, params$meddra_version,
                       params$ae_ctcae_version)
h <- hys_screen(tm$adlb, S$hys_window, S$alp_convention)
q <- qtc_screen(tm$adeg)
ds <- dlt_state(tm)
cs <- cohort_summary(tm)
roll <- trialmon_rollup(tm, S)
dosed <- ds[ds$N > 0, ]
ctcae_note <- sprintf("Lab grades: NCI CTCAE v%s.", S$ctcae)
ae_grade_note <- sprintf("AE grades as recorded by the investigator (NCI CTCAE v%s)", S$ae_ctcae)
meddra_note <- sprintf("Adverse events coded with MedDRA v%s (primary SOC). %s; they are data and are not re-derived when the lab-grading version (v%s here) changes.",
                       S$meddra, ae_grade_note, S$ctcae)
alp_note <- if (S$alp_convention) "ALP < 2x ULN in the draw with that aminotransferase elevation is also required (an SAP convention)." else
  "ALP is shown but not used to exclude a case; the SAP option ALP < 2x ULN is off."
E6R3 <- paste("ICH E6(R3) (Step 4 6 Jan 2025; EU effective 23 Jul 2025; FDA final guidance Sep 2025);",
              "Annex 2 Step 4 3 Jun 2026 (CHMP 25 Jun 2026, EU effective 15 Jan 2027; FDA: draft guidance Dec 2024, not final)")

# the findings the text cites, computed from the same objects as the tables
and_list <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) paste(x, collapse = "") else
  paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
coh_name <- function(cc) sub("^C", "Cohort ", cc)
who <- function(id) { s <- tm$adsl[match(id, tm$adsl$USUBJID), ]; sprintf("%s (%s, %g mg)", id, coh_name(s$COHORT), s$DOSEMG) }
is_dlt <- function(id) tm$adsl$DLTFL[match(id, tm$adsl$USUBJID)] == "Y"
pend <- tm$adsl[tm$adsl$DLTADJ == "Pending", ]
hys_ids <- h$USUBJID[h$hys]
conf_ids <- h$USUBJID[!h$hys & !is.na(h$at3x_day)]
hys_doses <- unique(tm$adsl$DOSEMG[tm$adsl$USUBJID %in% hys_ids])
pend_txt <- vapply(pend$USUBJID, function(id) {
  x <- q[q$USUBJID == id, ]
  if (nrow(x) && x$gt500) sprintf("%s had QTcF %d ms on Day %d (baseline %d ms). Under the synthetic protocol, QTcF above 500 ms is a candidate DLT; the event has not been adjudicated",
                                  who(id), x$max_qtcf, x$max_day, x$base)
  else sprintf("%s has a candidate DLT that has not been adjudicated: %s", who(id), pend$DLTDESC[pend$USUBJID == id])
}, "")
tag <- function(ids) ifelse(is_dlt(ids), paste(ids, "(an adjudicated DLT)"), ids)
liver_txt <- c(
  if (length(hys_ids)) sprintf("%s %s the potential Hy's Law screen", and_list(tag(hys_ids)),
                               if (length(hys_ids) == 1) "meets" else "meet"),
  if (length(conf_ids)) sprintf("%s had ALT or AST above 3x ULN that needed confirmation", and_list(tag(conf_ids))))
if (!length(liver_txt)) liver_txt <- "No participant meets the potential Hy's Law screen or had ALT or AST above 3x ULN"
next_dose <- tm$cohorts[grepl("^Planned", tm$cohorts$STATUS), ][1, ]
top <- dosed[which.max(dosed$DOSEMG), ]
pend_coh <- ds[ds$PENDING > 0 & ds$STATE != ds$STATE_IF_DLT, ]
```

             sprintf("MedDRA v%s; NCI CTCAE v%s for lab grades (AE grades as recorded, v%s); potential Hy's Law window %g days; ALP < 2x ULN convention %s",
                     S$meddra, S$ctcae, S$ae_ctcae, S$hys_window, if (S$alp_convention) "on" else "off"),

# Liver tests {#liver-tests}

**Definition used.** A participant is a *potential Hy's Law* case when ALT or AST is at least 3x ULN
and total bilirubin (TBL) is above 2x ULN **on or after** the day of that aminotransferase elevation,
within `r S$hys_window` days of it (the window is an SAP convention). Every draw with ALT or AST at least
3x ULN opens its own window, so a second elevation weeks after the first is screened as well; the
tables report the first draw that qualifies. `r alp_note` This follows FDA,
*Drug-Induced Liver Injury: Premarketing Clinical Evaluation* (July 2009), which asks for TBL above
2x ULN "without initial findings of cholestasis (elevated serum ALP)" and for other causes to be ruled
out. The screen cannot rule out other causes; the medical monitor does. Separately, any ALT or AST
**above** 3x ULN calls for repeat ALT, AST, ALP and TBL within 48 to 72 hours to confirm it.

```{r edish, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=4.9, fig.alt="eDISH plot: peak ALT or AST against peak total bilirubin for each participant, log scales, with reference lines at 3x and 2x ULN."}
both(function(look) edish_plot(h, look))
```

[eDISH: each point is one participant's peak post-baseline ALT or AST against peak TBL. The peaks need
not come from the same draw, so the upper-right quadrant is a prompt to check timing, not a
classification. Lower right: aminotransferase elevation without TBL above 2x ULN. Upper left: TBL above
2x ULN without an aminotransferase elevation (cholestasis, Gilbert syndrome or other causes).]{.tm-foot}

```{r liver-tables, results='asis'}
x <- h[h$hys | h$hys_quadrant_only | !is.na(h$at3x_day), ]
x <- x[order(-x$hys, x$USUBJID), ]
coh <- tm$adsl$COHORT[match(x$USUBJID, tm$adsl$USUBJID)]
cat(html_table(data.frame(
  Participant = x$USUBJID, Cohort = coh,
  `Peak ALT / AST (x ULN)` = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", x$peak_alt, x$peak_ast),
  `ALT or AST >= 3x (day)` = x$at3_day, `ALP then (x ULN)` = sprintf("%.1f", x$alp_at3),
  `R ratio (pattern)` = ifelse(is.na(x$r_at3), "", sprintf("%.1f (%s)", x$r_at3, x$pattern)),
  `Peak TBL (x ULN)` = sprintf("%.1f", x$peak_tbl), `TBL > 2x on or after it (day)` = x$tbl_day,
  `Potential Hy's Law` = ifelse(x$hys, "Yes", "No"), Quadrant = sub(":.*", "", x$quadrant),
  check.names = FALSE),
  num = c("ALT or AST >= 3x (day)", "ALP then (x ULN)", "Peak TBL (x ULN)", "TBL > 2x on or after it (day)"),
  caption = "Participants with ALT or AST above 3x ULN, or in the upper-right quadrant"))
y <- h[!is.na(h$at3x_day), ]
cat(html_table(data.frame(
  Participant = y$USUBJID, `ALT or AST > 3x ULN (day)` = y$at3x_day, `Value (x ULN)` = sprintf("%.1f", y$at3x_value),
  `First full repeat panel (day)` = y$repeat_day, `Days later` = y$repeat_gap,
  `Within 48 to 72 h` = ifelse(is.na(y$repeat_gap), "no repeat", ifelse(y$repeat_gap <= 3, "Yes", "No")),
  `Repeat ALT or AST (x ULN)` = sprintf("%.1f", y$repeat_at), `FDA (2009) discontinuation consideration` = y$stop_reason,
  check.names = FALSE),
  num = c("ALT or AST > 3x ULN (day)", "Value (x ULN)", "First full repeat panel (day)", "Days later", "Repeat ALT or AST (x ULN)"),
  caption = "Confirmation of aminotransferase elevations above 3x ULN"))
```

[ALT or AST >= 3x (day): for a potential Hy's Law case, the draw that opens the qualifying window;
otherwise the first such draw. ALP and the R ratio are read from that draw. R ratio = (ALT/ULN)/(ALP/ULN)
(at the first draw with ALT at least 3x ULN if only AST reached 3x in that draw): 5 or more hepatocellular,
between 2 and 5 mixed, 2 or less cholestatic. "Within 48 to 72 h" is judged on study days (the data
carry days, not clock times), as 3 days or fewer. The FDA (2009) discontinuation considerations that
these data can show are ALT or AST above 8x ULN, above 5x ULN for more than 2 weeks, and above 3x ULN with
TBL above 2x ULN; INR and symptoms are not in these data.]{.tm-foot}

```{r traj-ids}
traj_ids <- head(x$USUBJID[x$hys | !is.na(x$at3x_day)], 4)
```

```{r traj, eval=length(traj_ids) > 0, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=3.4, fig.alt=paste0("Liver tests by study day for ", and_list(traj_ids), ", as multiples of ULN.")}
tr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(traj_ids, function(i) cbind(liver_trajectory(tm, i), USUBJID = i)))
tr$USUBJID <- factor(tr$USUBJID, levels = traj_ids)
both(function(look) trajectory_plot(tr, look, NULL) + facet_wrap(~USUBJID, nrow = 1))
```

# QTcF {#qtcf}

```{r qtc, results='asis'}
q$COHORT <- tm$adsl$COHORT[match(q$USUBJID, tm$adsl$USUBJID)]
cats <- c(`QTcF > 450 ms` = "gt450", `QTcF > 480 ms` = "gt480", `QTcF > 500 ms` = "gt500",
          `Change from baseline > 30 ms` = "chg30", `Change from baseline > 60 ms` = "chg60",
          `Baseline QTcF > 450 ms` = "base450")
grp <- c(split(q, q$COHORT), list(Total = q))
out <- data.frame(Category = names(cats), check.names = FALSE)
for (g in names(grp)) out[[sprintf("%s (N=%d)", g, nrow(grp[[g]]))]] <- vapply(cats, function(cc) npct(sum(grp[[g]][[cc]]), nrow(grp[[g]])), "")
cat(html_table(out, num = names(out)[-1], caption = "Participants by maximum post-baseline QTcF category"))
z <- q[q$gt450 | q$chg30, ]
cat(html_table(data.frame(Participant = z$USUBJID, Cohort = z$COHORT, `Baseline (ms)` = z$base,
  `Maximum (ms)` = z$max_qtcf, Day = z$max_day, `Maximum change (ms)` = z$max_chg, Screen = sev_html(z$sev),
  check.names = FALSE), num = c("Baseline (ms)", "Maximum (ms)", "Day", "Maximum change (ms)"), raw = "Screen",
  caption = "Participants in any category"))
```

[QTcF: Fridericia-corrected QT, triplicate mean. Categories per ICH E14 (May 2005), the E14 Q&A (R3)
(December 2015) and the E14/S7B Q&As (February 2022): maximum post-baseline value above 450, 480 and
500 ms, regardless of sex, and maximum increase from baseline above 30 and 60 ms. Categories are
cumulative and a value equal to a threshold is not above it. Baseline: Day 1 predose; post-baseline
values start at the Day 1 4 h post-dose ECG. Participants already above 450 ms at baseline:
`r sum(q$base450)` of `r nrow(q)`. A categorical summary is a screen; concentration-QTc modeling belongs in
a prespecified analysis.]{.tm-foot}

# Laboratory shifts

```{r shift, results='asis'}
s <- lab_shift(tm$adlb, S$ctcae)
cat(html_table(data.frame(Test = s$TERM, `Baseline grade` = s$BGRADE, N = s$N, `Worst grade 0` = s$G0,
  `1` = s$G1, `2` = s$G2, `3` = s$G3, `4` = s$G4, check.names = FALSE),
  num = c("Baseline grade", "N", "Worst grade 0", "1", "2", "3", "4"),
  caption = "Shift from baseline grade to worst post-baseline grade"))
g <- lab_grades(tm$adlb, S$ctcae); g <- g[!is.na(g$WGRADE) & g$WGRADE >= 3, ]
cat(html_table(data.frame(Participant = g$USUBJID, Test = g$TERM, `Baseline grade` = g$BGRADE,
  `Worst grade` = g$WGRADE, check.names = FALSE), num = c("Baseline grade", "Worst grade"),
  caption = "Worst post-baseline grade 3 or higher"))
```

[`r ctcae_note` Grades come from multiples of the ULN or LLN, or from fold over baseline where the term
says so, not from absolute values alone. Creatinine increased: under v6.0, fold over baseline applies
only when the baseline is below the LLN; under v5.0 the grade is the worse of the x ULN and fold-over-baseline
grades. The v6.0 cut points follow admiral 1.5.0 (`atoxgr_criteria_ctcv6`) and were not re-checked
against the NCI v6.0 workbook here; v5.0 follows the NCI v5.0 workbook (2017-11-27). Baseline grades use
reference-range criteria only. Hemoglobin grade 4 is a clinical judgment and is not derived from the
value.]{.tm-foot}

# Adverse events by SOC and preferred term

```{r ae, results='asis'}
a <- ae_soc_pt(tm); N <- attr(a, "N")
lab <- ifelse(a$PT == "", a$SOC, paste0("&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;", esc(a$PT)))
out <- data.frame(`System organ class / Preferred term` = lab, check.names = FALSE)
for (gname in names(N)) out[[sprintf("%s (N=%d)", gname, N[[gname]])]] <- npct(a[[gname]], N[[gname]])
cat(html_table(out, num = names(out)[-1], raw = "System organ class / Preferred term",
               row_class = ifelse(a$PT == "", "soc", ""), caption = "Treatment-emergent adverse events, participants"))
sae <- tm$adae[tm$adae$AESER == "Y", ]
cat(html_table(data.frame(Participant = sae$USUBJID, `Preferred term` = sae$AEDECOD, SOC = sae$AEBODSYS,
  Grade = sae$AETOXGR, Relationship = sae$AREL, `Onset (day)` = sae$ASTDY,
  Outcome = ifelse(is.na(sae$AENDY), "ongoing", paste("resolved Day", sae$AENDY)), check.names = FALSE),
  num = c("Grade", "Onset (day)"), caption = "Serious adverse events"))
```

[`r meddra_note` Participants are counted once per row; N is the number dosed in each cohort. SOCs and
preferred terms are sorted by the total number of participants. Preferred terms keep MedDRA's
spelling.]{.tm-foot}

# Study-level indicators

```{r study, results='asis'}
st <- study_signals(tm)
cat(html_table(data.frame(Indicator = st$INDICATOR, Value = paste(st$VALUE, st$UNIT), Level = sev_html(st$LEVEL),
  Range = st$RULE, Detail = st$DETAIL, Source = st$SOURCE, check.names = FALSE), raw = "Level"))
```

[Pre-specified acceptable ranges, as in ICH E6(R3) section 3.10.1.3 ("quality tolerance limits at the
trial level"): exceeding one triggers evaluation, not an automatic stop. The operational values are
synthetic. Every level in this packet rolls up worst-of: the participant and cohort tier is
`r roll$participant` and the study tier is `r roll$study`, so the overall screen is `r roll$overall`.]{.tm-foot}

# Dose escalation: data for the decision

```{r esc, results='asis'}
by_coh <- function(col) vapply(dosed$COHORT, function(cc) {
  ids <- tm$adsl$USUBJID[tm$adsl$COHORT == cc]; col(ids)
}, "")
cat(html_table(data.frame(
  `Dose (mg)` = dosed$DOSEMG, Cohort = dosed$COHORT, `DLT-evaluable` = dosed$EVALUABLE,
  `DLTs (confirmed + pending)` = sprintf("%d + %d", dosed$DLT, dosed$PENDING),
  `Potential Hy's Law` = by_coh(function(ids) as.character(sum(h$hys[h$USUBJID %in% ids]))),
  `ALT or AST > 3x ULN` = by_coh(function(ids) as.character(sum(!is.na(h$at3x_day[h$USUBJID %in% ids])))),
  `QTcF > 500 ms or change > 60 ms` = by_coh(function(ids) as.character(sum(q$gt500[q$USUBJID %in% ids] | q$chg60[q$USUBJID %in% ids]))),
  `Grade 3 or higher TEAE` = npct(cs$G3[cs$N > 0], cs$N[cs$N > 0]),
  check.names = FALSE),
  num = c("Dose (mg)", "DLT-evaluable", "DLTs (confirmed + pending)", "Potential Hy's Law", "ALT or AST > 3x ULN",
          "QTcF > 500 ms or change > 60 ms", "Grade 3 or higher TEAE"),
  caption = "Key findings by dose"))
cat(sprintf('<p class="tm-foot">Participants. Potential Hy\'s Law: window %g days, ALP option %s. Grade 3 or higher TEAE counts AE grades as recorded by the investigator (NCI CTCAE v%s).</p>\n',
            S$hys_window, if (S$alp_convention) "on" else "off", S$ae_ctcae))
cat(html_table(data.frame(Cohort = dosed$COHORT, `Dose (mg)` = dosed$DOSEMG,
  `Illustrative 3+3 rule reference` = dosed$text, check.names = FALSE), num = "Dose (mg)",
  caption = "What an illustrative 3+3 rule would say (a reference, not a recommendation)"))
```

**Reading the rule reference.** Under a 3+3 rule, 0 of 3 or 1 of 6 participants with a DLT is
escalation-eligible, 1 of 3 means the cohort expands to 6, and 2 or more mean the dose exceeds the
maximum tolerated dose; a dose can be called the MTD only with 6 participants treated at it.
`r if (nrow(pend_coh)) sprintf("For %s the reference depends on the committee's adjudication of %s.", and_list(coh_name(pend_coh$COHORT)), and_list(pend$USUBJID[pend$COHORT %in% pend_coh$COHORT])) else ""`
3+3 appears here only as an illustration: model-assisted designs such as BOIN (FDA fit-for-purpose
determination, December 2021, for the local BOIN design under a non-informative prior) are the current
alternative, and this example implements neither as a decision tool. A rule reference never replaces the
committee's review of the whole safety picture, including
`r if (length(hys_ids)) sprintf("the potential Hy's Law %s at %s", if (length(hys_ids) == 1) "case" else "cases", and_list(paste(hys_doses, "mg"))) else "the liver findings in Section 4"`.

**Options the synthetic protocol allows the committee to consider,** in protocol order: escalate to
`r if (is.na(next_dose$COHORT)) "the next planned dose" else paste(next_dose$DOSEMG, "mg")` as planned;
escalate to an intermediate dose; enroll further participants at `r top$DOSEMG` mg; stop escalation and
select a lower dose; pause dosing pending further evaluation. They are listed, not ranked.

::: {.tm-decision}
**Committee record** (completed by the committee, not by this packet)

`r if (nrow(pend)) paste0("DLT adjudication for ", and_list(pend$USUBJID), ":") else "DLT adjudications:"` ______________________________

Decision on dose escalation: ______________________________

Rationale: ______________________________

Chair: ______________________ Date: ______________________
:::

# Methods and conventions

- **Source.** The TRIALMON synthetic dataset (`adsl`, `adlb`, `adeg`, `adae`, `cohorts`, `study_kri`),
  written by `R/gen_data.R` from one seed. Every table is computed at render time by `R/logic.R`, the
  code behind the TRIALMON console and its tests, and the findings the text cites (participants, values,
  days and counts) are computed from the same objects. The study design and the protocol's options are
  fixed text from the synthetic protocol.
- **Populations.** Safety population: all dosed participants. Baseline: the Day 1 predose value.
  Post-baseline: labs after Day 1; ECGs from the Day 1 4 h post-dose time point on; both include
  unscheduled draws.
- **Counting.** Participants are counted once per row of a table. Percentages use the dosed
  participants in the column.
- **Dictionaries and grading.** MedDRA v`r S$meddra`; NCI CTCAE v`r S$ctcae` for laboratory grades,
  derived from the values; AE grades as recorded by the investigator under NCI CTCAE v`r S$ae_ctcae` (a
  property of the data: changing the lab-grading version does not re-grade an AE). All three are
  parameters of this document (`meddra_version`, `ctcae_version`, `ae_ctcae_version`), as are the Hy's
  Law window (`hys_window_days`) and the ALP convention (`alp_convention`).
- **Guidance cited.** FDA, *Drug-Induced Liver Injury: Premarketing Clinical Evaluation* (July 2009);
  ICH E14 (May 2005), E14 Q&A (R3) (10 Dec 2015) and E14/S7B Q&As (Step 4 21 Feb 2022); NCI CTCAE
  v`r S$ctcae`; `r E6R3`.
- **What was executed.** Rendered with Quarto and `r R.version.string` on synthetic data; the rules are
  covered by testthat tests (rule boundaries, the shipped study and the Shiny server). No validated system
  or independent programmer produced or checked these numbers.
- **What a real packet adds.** Tables from validated programs on ADaM, a named statistician's sign-off,
  and, for a DSMB with access to unblinded comparisons, open and closed sections with an independent
  reporting statistician. This open-label example has no closed section.
